display.title: The Trip to the Baal Shem Tov's Melave Malka
display.summary_short: A Chassid sets out through a blizzard to join the Baal Shem Tov's Melave Malka and gets a ride from a singing wagon driver who turns out to be Eliyahu HaNavi.
display.summary_long: The recording joins a teaching already under way: the Rebbe taught that in our generation we should fill our lives with good deeds, like bringing clean furniture into a house, and the darkness leaves by itself. The Midrash says the Parah Adumah was prepared by Elazar, whose name means 'G-d helps', because we do our part and Hashem helps. Then a story of the Baal Shem Tov. A Chassid who lives just across a small forest from Mezhibuzh joins the Baal Shem Tov for Melave Malka every Motzaei Shabbos. One week, in a heavy blizzard, he falls into an icy pit, goes home to change, and sets out again. A wagon full of rattling pots and pans picks him up, and the driver makes him sing along all the way. When he arrives, the Baal Shem Tov calls him to the front and asks how it felt to sing zemiros with Eliyahu HaNavi. The storyteller connects this to the coming of Pesach and good resolutions, and explains the Rebbe's instruction that everyone should have a mashpia, with a story of a Chassid who wanted only the Rebbe's own answer.
display.lesson: When you are determined to do what is right, Hashem helps you: do your best and Hashem will do the rest. Follow the Rebbe's instructions, including having a mashpia, to receive his brachos.
